title: What do you press to go up four floors and down three?
description: The lift has a plus button for up and a minus button for down, and each press moves it one floor. The presses for four floors up and three floors down are counted and written with their signs. Keeko thinks pressing minus three times gives the plain number three, and the lift going down breaks that doubt.
teaching_notes: One idea: a press is one floor, and the sign in front tells whether the lift goes up or down. Watch for students who write only the count of presses and drop the sign.

source: What do you press to go four floors up? What do you press to
video_script.why: A child learns to write lift presses as signed numbers, because every later floor number and movement uses the same signs.
video_script.substitution: the book's own lift with a plus button and a minus button, going four floors up and three floors down
video_script.anchor: the lift of Ruhee with its plus button and minus button, one press for one floor
video_script.wrong_answer: pressing minus three times gives the number three
video_script.wrong_move: writes only the count of presses and drops the minus sign
video_script.payoff_line: The sign tells us if the lift goes up or down.

final_answer.value: Four floors up: + + + + or +4. Three floors down: − − − or −3.
final_answer.spoken: plus four presses for four floors up, and minus three presses for three floors down

names.Ruhee: the multi-storey block of floors above and below the ground, used as the model for integers

hold_back: Answer: four floors up, + + + + or +4; three floors down, − − − or −3
never_show: any floor number of a shop
maths_rules: Each plus press moves the lift one floor up; each minus press moves it one floor down.
Four floors up needs four plus presses, written +4.
Three floors down needs three minus presses, written −3.
video_script.design: One idea: a press is one floor and the sign gives the direction. One lift picture throughout; the pressed buttons light up one by one. Keeko's doubt is broken by the lift going down.

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks pressing minus three times gives the number three, because we only count the presses.

<bookmark mark='fix'/>The minus sign must stay, because it says the lift moved down.
